scope: patching body[164] did NOT change the entity count, because the two gate bits are read BEFORE the count and one of them fails
what_happened: the byte cursor is still 164 and the length still 172, so the patched byte was in the right place for a BYTE read
but the count is still 0 - because 0x671650 reads TWO GATE BITS before it ever calls the count reader
and the state moved from 10 to 9, which proves the patched byte DOES participate in the parse - it just is not the count's source at this point
the_conclusion: the count cannot be reached until bit 1 (0x671678) and bit 2 (0x671685) both read as 1
our bodies fail one of those gates, so the count reader is never called
therefore the byte-164 experiment was premature: it tested a byte the decoder never asks for
the_missing_piece: the BIT cursor position at 0x671650 entry, which tells us exactly which two bits are the gates
the Cursor probe reads [+0x14], [+0x18], [+0x1C] and [+0x24] but none of those is the bit cursor
so the next step is to read 0x447190 (the bit reader) and find which stream field it advances
next: disassemble 0x447190 to identify the bit cursor field
then extend the Cursor probe to log it, which gives the exact bit indices of the two gates and, after them, of the count
